## Motivation

Add support for LiLiCorr GGUF draft checkpoints, including `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB-LiLiCorr-GGUF`.

Depends on #44563. This branch includes those changes and should be rebased onto main once it merges.

## Modifications

- Read LiLiCorr configuration and tensor mappings from GGUF metadata.
- Load packed NVFP4 weights through the existing ModelOpt implementation.
- Limit detection to GGUF checkpoints with DFlash architecture and LiLiCorr metadata.
- Add regression tests, serving tests, and a documented launch example.

NVFP4 Marlin LiLiCorr heads currently require TP1. This is an existing restriction in the LiLiCorr implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested commit `653e968` with the 24GB quantized target on one H100 and the BF16 target on one B300, both at TP1. Both targets used the same published 24GB LiLiCorr drafters, in safetensors and GGUF formats, with unchanged configs. Results were nearly identical

| Target / GPU | Drafter format | GSM8K | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24GB quant / H100 | Safetensors | 174/200 (87%) | 6.00 |
| 24GB quant / H100 | GGUF | 174/200 (87%) | 6.00 |
| BF16 / B300 | Safetensors | 173/200 (86.5%) | 6.10 |
| BF16 / B300 | GGUF | 173/200 (86.5%) | 6.10 |

All runs used DFLASH block size 8: seven proposed draft tokens plus one target/bonus token. Acceptance length includes the bonus token and is averaged over the 200 per-request values.

Both formats passed text, image-counting, and OCR smoke checks with both targets. All 54 focused regression tests passed in the H100 validation.

GSM8K used the legacy `sglang.test.run_eval` chat evaluator with 200 examples, zero shots, temperature 0, one evaluation worker, a 512-token output limit, and thinking disabled. The one-question difference is not meaningful evidence of an accuracy difference.

EDIT: After the review updates, the registered E2E test uses `sgl_eval` with thinking disabled and a prompt requesting calculations followed by a boxed final answer. On the H100 with the 24GB target and GGUF drafter, it scored 192/200 (96%).

A comparison run using `sgl_eval` with the prompt and answer extractor used with `run_eval` scored 175/200 (87.5%), consistent with the original 87% result. The new 96% score uses different prompting and grading.

The commands below reproduce the original H100 validation using the legacy `run_eval` evaluator.

```bash
target=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB
target_revision=5165e12246e823a578bc2d483958439c38d9d6bd
draft=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB-LiLiCorr-GGUF
draft_revision=182d2987939e12f458298b5d5f6ef98912f4ad6c

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$target" --revision "$target_revision" \
  --served-model-name validation --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 4096 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-mamba-cache-size 32 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path "$draft" \
  --speculative-draft-model-revision "$draft_revision" \
  --speculative-dflash-block-size 8 \
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend triton
```

BF16 validation used target revision `a6a1e5030819a130a1ea08aadb1fe42f4cc86777` of `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16` and `--mem-fraction-static 0.92`, with the same drafter revisions and remaining server settings.

For the safetensors drafter, substitute these values before launching:

```bash
draft=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB-LiLiCorr
draft_revision=449d24140160b8e51871bfc0f0a7338abf640aa1
```

Run the updated `sgl_eval` evaluation from the repository root against the running server:

```bash
python3 -m sgl_eval.cli run gsm8k \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --model validation \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 4 \
  --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --top-p 1 \
  --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false \
  --prompt test/registered/e2e/speculative/gsm8k_worked_solution.yaml \
  --out-dir sgl-eval-gsm8k
```

The original accuracy results above used this legacy `run_eval` command:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api chat --model validation \
  --num-examples 200 --num-shots 0 --num-threads 1 \
  --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same H100 and server settings as above. The target-only baseline omits the five speculative options.

Synthetic requests used 256 input tokens and 128 output tokens, with 20 requests at concurrency 1 and 40 at concurrency 4. All requests completed.

| Drafter | Concurrency | Output tokens/s | Input + output tokens/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| None | 1 | 89.6 | 268.7 |
| Safetensors | 1 | 107.6 | 322.8 |
| GGUF | 1 | 107.9 | 323.8 |
| None | 4 | 138.1 | 414.3 |
| Safetensors | 4 | 153.8 | 461.4 |
| GGUF | 4 | 156.7 | 470.1 |

Run against each server configuration, using a separate output directory for each:

```bash
target=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB

for concurrency in 1 4; do
  requests=20
  if [ "$concurrency" = 4 ]; then requests=40; fi

  python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
    --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
    --model "$target" --tokenizer "$target" \
    --served-model-name validation \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 \
    --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$requests" \
    --max-concurrency "$concurrency" \
    --warmup-requests 2 --flush-cache --tokenize-prompt \
    --seed 42 --temperature 0 \
    --output-file "c${concurrency}.jsonl"
done
```

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`lru_cache` keeps each parsed `GGUFReader` alive for the life of the process. The reader holds every metadata part as a NumPy view, so the drafter's tokenizer metadata stays in host memory after config and weight loading finish. The main process (`_resolve_speculative_algorithm_alias` -> `get_config`) and the scheduler each keep one. `build_gguf_tokenizer` now also caches the reader for GGUF-native targets such as muse-glimmer, in every process that builds the tokenizer.

**Example**

On a synthetic GGUF with the drafter's 131k tokens and 269k merges, one live reader adds about 470 MB RSS. Freeing it releases about 400 MB.

**Fix**

Cache the small derived results (architecture, LiLiCorr check, built config) instead of the reader, and let `lilicorr_gguf_weights` open a short-lived reader. Or call `get_gguf_reader.cache_clear()` once loading finishes.

+You can also pass a local `.gguf` file as the draft path. The GGUF loader supports NVFP4 weights with 16-bit activations and dense F32 or BF16 tensors. It repacks the NVFP4 weights at load time without dequantizing them. NVFP4A16 LiLiCorr heads use Marlin and currently require tensor parallelism 1. This drafter uses attention sinks; the example selects Triton for draft attention because it supports them.
+
 **Use a backend that opts out of the host `seq_lens` mirror.** `AttentionBackend.needs_cpu_seq_lens` defaults to `True`; `fa3`, `triton`, `trtllm_mha`, `trtllm_mla`, `flashmla` and `dsa` set it `False`, while `FlashInferAttnBackend` inherits the default. Under a backend that does not opt out the worker publishes `seq_lens_cpu` every step, which is a device-to-host sync per block. The flag is OR-ed over the target and draft runners, so both have to opt out. This is a property of DFlash decoding rather than of LiLiCorr, but it dominates the throughput of a 16-slot block. Backends also differ in attention numerics, so acceptance measured on different backends does not belong in one table.
 
 A checkpoint carrying head weights but declaring `architectures: ["DFlashDraftModel"]` loads as plain DFlash and ignores the head, which reads as a small acceptance loss rather than an error. The reverse, declaring `LiLiCorrDraftModel` without complete head weights, is refused at load.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the SGLang project
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# Adapted from: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9cede34a674c392092134e34218b127d6bbb3679/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt_block_quant.py
+"""Load ModelOpt safetensors blocks with the existing GGUF kernels.
+
+Supported formats:
+- Linear layers: Q8_0 and IQ2_XXS.
+- MoE experts: IQ2_XXS, with gated SiLU or ungated ReLU2.
+
+Weights use [N, K / block_size, block_bytes] per linear layer or expert.
+Gated experts store gate/up in separate w13 halves. TP keeps blocks intact.
+Large expert batches are split to stay within the CUDA vector-kernel grid limit.
+Expert placement must be trivial. EP, EPLB, redundant experts, fused shared
+experts and presharded expert weights are unsupported.
+Q8_0 experts are rejected. Other GGML codecs are not enabled by this adapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.parameter import ModelWeightParameter
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.base_config import (
+    FusedMoEMethodBase,
+    LinearMethodBase,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.fused_moe_triton import FusedMoE
+    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.base import MoeRunnerConfig
+    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher import (
+        CombineInput,
+        StandardDispatchOutput,
+    )
+
+
+def ggml_block_layout(quant_algo: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    from gguf import GGML_QUANT_SIZES, GGMLQuantizationType
+
+    quant_type = GGMLQuantizationType[quant_algo]
+    block_size, block_bytes = GGML_QUANT_SIZES[quant_type]
+    return block_size, block_bytes, int(quant_type)
+
+
+def validate_ggml_recipe(quant_algo: str, recipe: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    block_size, block_bytes, _ = ggml_block_layout(quant_algo)
+    if (
+        recipe.get("group_size") != block_size
+        or recipe.get("block_payload_bytes") != block_bytes
+        or recipe.get("packing") != "ggml"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid {quant_algo} GGML block layout: {recipe}")
+
+
+class ModelOptGGMLLinearMethod(LinearMethodBase):
+    """Retain checkpoint blocks and the standard linear weight-loader contract."""
+
+    def __init__(self, quant_algo: str) -> None:
+        self.block_size, self.block_bytes, self.quant_type = ggml_block_layout(
+            quant_algo
+        )
+
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        input_size_per_partition: int,
+        output_partition_sizes: list[int],
+        input_size: int,
+        output_size: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs: Any,
+    ) -> None:
+        if input_size_per_partition % self.block_size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "GGML input partition must contain whole quantization blocks"
+            )
+        layer.register_parameter(
+            "weight",
+            ModelWeightParameter(
+                data=torch.empty(
+                    sum(output_partition_sizes),
+                    input_size_per_partition // self.block_size,
+                    self.block_bytes,
+                    dtype=torch.uint8,
+                ),
+                input_dim=1,
+                output_dim=0,
+                weight_loader=extra_weight_attrs["weight_loader"],
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.gguf import fused_mul_mat_gguf
+
+        output = fused_mul_mat_gguf(
+            x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1]),
+            layer.weight.flatten(1),
+            self.quant_type,
+        )
+        if bias is not None:
+            output.add_(bias)
+        return output.view(*x.shape[:-1], layer.weight.shape[0])
+
+
+class ModelOptGGMLMoEMethod(FusedMoEMethodBase):
+    """Packed expert blocks with tensor-parallel loading and GGUF execution."""
+
+    # GGUF applies the routing weights during the final expert reduction.
+    fuse_routed_scaling_factor_in_topk = True
+
+    def __init__(self, quant_algo: str) -> None:
+        self.block_size, self.block_bytes, self.quant_type = ggml_block_layout(
+            quant_algo
+        )
+
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: FusedMoE,
+        num_experts: int,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        intermediate_size_per_partition: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs: Any,
+    ) -> None:
+        moe = get_exec().moe
+        if (
+            layer.moe_ep_size != 1
+            or moe.enable_eplb
+            or moe.init_expert_location != "trivial"
+            or moe.ep_num_redundant_experts > 0
+            or layer.num_fused_shared_experts
+            or layer.use_presharded_weights
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "ModelOpt GGML experts require trivial expert placement without EP, "
+                "EPLB, redundant experts, fused shared experts, or presharded weights"
+            )
+        if extra_weight_attrs.get("with_bias", False):
+            raise ValueError("ModelOpt GGML experts do not support bias")
+        if (
+            hidden_size % self.block_size
+            or intermediate_size_per_partition % self.block_size
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "GGML expert partitions must contain whole quantization blocks"
+            )
+
+        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
+        self.intermediate_size = intermediate_size_per_partition
+        self.tp_rank = layer.moe_tp_rank
+        self.tp_size = layer.moe_tp_size
+        self.is_gated = layer.moe_runner_config.is_gated
+        for name, rows, columns in (
+            (
+                "w13_weight",
+                (2 if self.is_gated else 1) * self.intermediate_size,
+                hidden_size,
+            ),
+            ("w2_weight", hidden_size, self.intermediate_size),
+        ):
+            layer.register_parameter(
+                name,
+                ModelWeightParameter(
+                    data=torch.empty(
+                        num_experts,
+                        rows,
+                        columns // self.block_size,
+                        self.block_bytes,
+                        dtype=torch.uint8,
+                    ),
+                    input_dim=2,
+                    output_dim=1,
+                    weight_loader=self.weight_loader,
+                ),
+            )
+
+    def weight_loader(
+        self,
+        param: torch.nn.Parameter,
+        loaded_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        weight_name: str,
+        shard_id: str,
+        expert_id: int | None,
+        return_success: bool = False,
+    ) -> bool | None:
+        if shard_id not in ("w1", "w2", "w3") or (
+            not self.is_gated and shard_id == "w3"
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid GGML expert projection {shard_id}")
+        if expert_id is None or not 0 <= expert_id < param.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid GGML expert index {expert_id}")
+        global_intermediate = self.intermediate_size * self.tp_size
+        expected = (
+            (self.hidden_size, global_intermediate // self.block_size, self.block_bytes)
+            if shard_id == "w2"
+            else (
+                global_intermediate,
+                self.hidden_size // self.block_size,
+                self.block_bytes,
+            )
+        )
+        if loaded_weight.dtype != torch.uint8 or tuple(loaded_weight.shape) != expected:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Invalid packed tensor {weight_name}: expected uint8{expected}, "
+                f"got {loaded_weight.dtype}{tuple(loaded_weight.shape)}"
+            )
+
+        destination = param.data[expert_id]
+        if shard_id == "w2":
+            size = self.intermediate_size // self.block_size
+            source = loaded_weight.narrow(1, self.tp_rank * size, size)
+        else:
+            size = self.intermediate_size
+            source = loaded_weight.narrow(0, self.tp_rank * size, size)
+            destination = destination.narrow(0, size if shard_id == "w3" else 0, size)
+        destination.copy_(source)
+        return True if return_success else None
+
+    def create_moe_runner(
+        self, layer: FusedMoE, moe_runner_config: MoeRunnerConfig
+    ) -> None:
+        if (moe_runner_config.is_gated and moe_runner_config.activation != "silu") or (
+            not moe_runner_config.is_gated and moe_runner_config.activation != "relu2"
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "ModelOpt GGML experts require gated SiLU or ungated ReLU2; "
+                f"got activation={moe_runner_config.activation!r}, "
+                f"is_gated={moe_runner_config.is_gated}"
+            )
+        if moe_runner_config.no_combine:
+            raise ValueError("ModelOpt GGML experts do not support no_combine=True")
+        if moe_runner_config.apply_router_weight_on_input:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "ModelOpt GGML experts do not support applying router weights to inputs"
+            )
+        activation_parameters = {
+            "gemm1_alpha": moe_runner_config.gemm1_alpha,
+            "gemm1_beta": moe_runner_config.gemm1_beta,
+            "gemm1_clamp_limit": moe_runner_config.gemm1_clamp_limit,
+            "swiglu_limit": moe_runner_config.swiglu_limit,
+        }
+        custom_parameters = [
+            name for name, value in activation_parameters.items() if value is not None
+        ]
+        if custom_parameters:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "ModelOpt GGML experts do not support custom activation parameters: "
+                + ", ".join(custom_parameters)
+            )
+        self.moe_runner_config = moe_runner_config
+
+    def apply(
+        self, layer: FusedMoE, dispatch_output: StandardDispatchOutput
+    ) -> CombineInput:
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher import StandardCombineInput
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import BypassedTopKOutput
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.gguf import fused_moe_gguf
+
+        topk_output = dispatch_output.topk_output
+        if isinstance(topk_output, BypassedTopKOutput):
+            topk_output = topk_output.to_standard(layer_id=layer.layer_id)
+        # GGUF kernels read expert IDs as int32.
+        topk_ids = topk_output.topk_ids.to(torch.int32)
+
+        def apply_weights(x, weights, ids):
+            return fused_moe_gguf(
+                x=x,
+                w1=layer.w13_weight.flatten(-2),
+                w2=layer.w2_weight.flatten(-2),
+                topk_weights=weights,
+                topk_ids=ids,
+                qweight_type=self.quant_type,
+                qweight_type2=self.quant_type,
+                activation=self.moe_runner_config.activation,
+                is_gated=self.moe_runner_config.is_gated,
+            )
+
+        x, weights = dispatch_output.hidden_states, topk_output.topk_weights
+        # The vector kernel needs one grid-z entry per token-expert pair.
+        chunk_size = 65535 // topk_ids.shape[1]
+        if x.shape[0] <= chunk_size:
+            output = apply_weights(x, weights, topk_ids)
+        else:
+            output = torch.cat(
+                [
+                    apply_weights(
+                        x[start : start + chunk_size],
+                        weights[start : start + chunk_size],
+                        topk_ids[start : start + chunk_size],
+                    )
+                    for start in range(0, x.shape[0], chunk_size)
+                ],
+                dim=0,
+            )
+        return StandardCombineInput(hidden_states=output)

+"""Read DFlash LiLiCorr GGUF exports using the existing NVFP4A16 runtime.
+
+NVFP4 blocks are repacked at load time without dequantization. Dense tensors
+keep their exported values. GGUF's materialized lattice bias is converted to
+an equivalent slot-relative bias for the existing LiLiCorr head.
+"""
+
+import re
+from copy import deepcopy
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+from transformers import Qwen3Config

+_BACKBONE_NAMES = {
+    "ffn_down": "mlp.down_proj",
+    "ffn_gate": "mlp.gate_proj",
+    "ffn_up": "mlp.up_proj",
+    "attn_norm": "input_layernorm",
+    "ffn_norm": "post_attention_layernorm",
+    "attn_sinks.weight": "self_attn.attention_sink_bias",
+    "attn_k_norm": "self_attn.k_norm",
+    "attn_q_norm": "self_attn.q_norm",
+    "attn_k": "self_attn.k_proj",
+    "attn_q": "self_attn.q_proj",
+    "attn_v": "self_attn.v_proj",
+    "attn_output": "self_attn.o_proj",
+    "attn_conv_base": "attention_conv.base_kernel",
+    "ffn_conv_base": "mlp_conv.base_kernel",
+    "attn_conv_proj": "attention_conv.kernel_projection",
+    "ffn_conv_proj": "mlp_conv.kernel_projection",
+}
+_HEAD_NAMES = {
+    "attn_output": "attn.out_proj",
+    "ffn_down": "mlp.down_proj",
+    "ffn_up": "mlp.up_proj",
+    "attn_norm": "attn_norm",
+    "ffn_norm": "mlp_norm",
+}
+_FEATURE_NAMES = {
+    "ffn_down": "feature_mlp.down_proj",
+    "ffn_up": "feature_mlp.up_proj",
+    "ffn_norm": "feature_norm",
+}
+
+
+def lilicorr_tensor_name(name: str, num_layers: int, num_head_layers: int) -> str:
+    match = re.fullmatch(r"blk\.(\d+)\.(.+)", name)
+    if match:
+        layer, tail = int(match[1]), match[2]
+        if layer < num_layers:
+            names, prefix = _BACKBONE_NAMES, f"layers.{layer}."
+        elif layer < num_layers + num_head_layers:
+            names, prefix = _HEAD_NAMES, f"lilicorr.layers.{layer - num_layers}."
+        elif layer == num_layers + num_head_layers:
+            names, prefix = _FEATURE_NAMES, "lilicorr."
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected LiLiCorr GGUF layer: {name}")
+        for source, target in names.items():
+            if tail == source or tail.startswith(source + "."):
+                return prefix + target + tail[len(source) :]
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown LiLiCorr GGUF tensor: {name}")
+    if name == "enc.output_norm.weight":
+        return "hidden_norm.weight"
+    if name == "output_norm.weight":
+        return "norm.weight"
+    if name in ("lilicorr.rank_embedding.weight", "lilicorr.slot_embedding.weight"):
+        return name.removesuffix(".weight")
+    if name not in ("fc.weight", "fc.scale") and not name.startswith("lilicorr."):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown LiLiCorr GGUF tensor: {name}")
+    return name.replace(".attn.in_proj.weight", ".attn.in_proj_weight").replace(
+        ".attn.in_proj.bias", ".attn.in_proj_bias"
+    )
+
+
+def build_lilicorr_gguf_config(path: str) -> Qwen3Config:
+    """Keep caller overrides separate from cached checkpoint metadata."""
+    return Qwen3Config(**deepcopy(_read_lilicorr_gguf_config(path)))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
+def _read_lilicorr_gguf_config(path: str) -> dict:
+    from gguf import GGMLQuantizationType, GGUFReader
+
+    reader = GGUFReader(path, mode="r")
+
+    def field(key):
+        if key not in reader.fields:
+            raise ValueError(f"LiLiCorr GGUF is missing metadata {key!r}")
+        return reader.fields[key].contents()
+
+    if field("general.architecture") != "dflash":
+        raise ValueError("Expected a DFlash GGUF checkpoint")
+    activation_precision = reader.fields.get("general.tensor_extra.prec_a4")
+    if activation_precision is not None and any(activation_precision.contents()):
+        raise ValueError("LiLiCorr GGUF loading requires 16-bit activations")
+    layers = int(field("dflash.block_count"))
+    head_layers = int(field("lilicorr.num_layers"))
+    hidden = int(field("lilicorr.hidden_size"))
+    block = int(field("dflash.block_size"))
+    targets = [int(i) - 1 for i in field("dflash.target_layers")]
+    # GGUF counts the embedding output; SGLang captures decoder layer inputs.
+    if not targets or min(targets) < 0:
+        raise ValueError("LiLiCorr GGUF target layers must be positive")
+    dflash = {
+        "mask_token_id": int(field("tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id")),
+        "target_layer_ids": targets,
+        "causal": bool(field("dflash.attention.causal")),
+        "attention_sink_bias": any(".attn_sinks." in t.name for t in reader.tensors),
+        "projector_type": "lilicorr",
+        "lilicorr_enabled": True,
+        "lilicorr_mlp_ratio": int(field("lilicorr.mlp_hidden_size")) / hidden,
+    }
+    for key in ("conv_kernel_size", "conv_group_size"):
+        dflash[key] = int(field("dflash." + key))
+    for key in (
+        "hidden_size",
+        "candidate_topk",
+        "num_heads",
+        "num_layers",
+        "factor_dim",
+        "vector_eps",
+        "logit_scale",
+    ):
+        dflash["lilicorr_" + key] = field("lilicorr." + key)
+    excluded = []
+    for tensor in reader.tensors:
+        name = lilicorr_tensor_name(tensor.name, layers, head_layers)
+        if tensor.tensor_type not in (
+            GGMLQuantizationType.NVFP4,
+            GGMLQuantizationType.F32,
+            GGMLQuantizationType.BF16,
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unsupported LiLiCorr GGUF tensor type: {tensor.tensor_type}"
+            )
+        if (
+            tensor.name.endswith(".weight")
+            and tensor.tensor_type != GGMLQuantizationType.NVFP4
+        ):
+            # Keep dense weights out of the NVFP4 path.
+            excluded.append(name.removesuffix(".weight"))
+    window = int(field("dflash.attention.sliding_window"))
+    pattern = field("dflash.attention.sliding_window_pattern")
+    if len(pattern) != layers:
+        raise ValueError("LiLiCorr GGUF sliding-window pattern must cover each layer")
+    return dict(
+        architectures=["LiLiCorrDraftModel"],
+        hidden_size=int(field("dflash.embedding_length")),
+        intermediate_size=int(field("dflash.feed_forward_length")),
+        num_hidden_layers=layers,
+        num_attention_heads=int(field("dflash.attention.head_count")),
+        num_key_value_heads=int(field("dflash.attention.head_count_kv")),
+        head_dim=int(field("dflash.attention.key_length")),
+        max_position_embeddings=int(field("dflash.context_length")),
+        rms_norm_eps=float(field("dflash.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon")),
+        rope_theta=float(field("dflash.rope.freq_base")),
+        vocab_size=len(field("tokenizer.ggml.tokens")),
+        layer_types=[
+            "sliding_attention" if sliding else "full_attention" for sliding in pattern
+        ],
+        sliding_window=window,
+        use_sliding_window=any(pattern),
+        block_size=block,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        dflash_config=dflash,
+        quantization_config={
+            "quant_method": "modelopt_fp4",
+            "quant_algo": "W4A16_NVFP4",
+            "group_size": 16,
+            "ignore": excluded,
+        },
+    )
+
+
+def repack_nvfp4(data, shape):
+    import numpy as np
+    import torch
+
+    if len(shape) != 2 or int(shape[0]) % 64:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"NVFP4 GGUF requires a matrix with K divisible by 64, got {shape}"
+        )
+    k, rows = map(int, shape)
+    blocks = np.asarray(data).reshape(rows, k // 64, 36)
+    scales = blocks[:, :, :4].copy().reshape(rows, k // 16)
+    if np.any(scales > 127):
+        raise ValueError("NVFP4 GGUF scales must use unsigned E4M3")
+    scales[scales == 127] = 0
+    packed = blocks[:, :, 4:].reshape(rows, k // 16, 8)
+    # GGUF packs the two halves of each group; ModelOpt packs adjacent values.
+    codes = np.concatenate([packed & 15, packed >> 4], axis=-1)
+    weight = (codes[..., ::2] | (codes[..., 1::2] << 4)).reshape(rows, k // 2)
+    return torch.from_numpy(weight.copy()), torch.from_numpy(scales).view(
+        torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+
+
+def slot_bias_from_gguf(bias, block_size: int, topk: int):
+    import torch
+
+    slots = block_size - 1
+    if tuple(bias.shape[1:]) != (slots * topk, slots * topk):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected LiLiCorr GGUF attention bias shape: {bias.shape}")
+    relative = bias.new_zeros((bias.shape[0], 2 * block_size - 1))
+    for offset in range(-(slots - 1), slots):
+        relative[:, offset + block_size - 1] = bias[
+            :, max(offset, 0) * topk, max(-offset, 0) * topk
+        ]
+    ids = torch.arange(slots).repeat_interleave(topk)
+    rebuilt = relative[:, ids[:, None] - ids[None, :] + block_size - 1]
+    if not torch.equal(rebuilt, bias):
+        raise ValueError("LiLiCorr GGUF attention bias is not slot-relative")
+    # The export already combines the relative and same-slot terms.
+    return relative, bias.new_zeros(bias.shape[0])
+
+
+def lilicorr_gguf_weights(path: str, config):
+    import numpy as np
+    import torch
+    from gguf import GGMLQuantizationType, GGUFReader
+
+    reader = GGUFReader(path, mode="r")
+    head = config.dflash_config
+    layers, head_layers = config.num_hidden_layers, head["lilicorr_num_layers"]
+    tensors = {t.name: t for t in reader.tensors}
+    for tensor in reader.tensors:
+        name = lilicorr_tensor_name(tensor.name, layers, head_layers)
+        if name.endswith(".scale"):
+            continue
+        if tensor.tensor_type == GGMLQuantizationType.NVFP4:
+            weight, scale = repack_nvfp4(tensor.data, tensor.shape)
+            scale_tensor = tensors.get(tensor.name.removesuffix(".weight") + ".scale")
+            if (
+                scale_tensor is None
+                or scale_tensor.tensor_type != GGMLQuantizationType.F32
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"NVFP4 GGUF tensor {tensor.name} requires an F32 global scale"
+                )
+            global_scale = torch.from_numpy(
+                np.array(scale_tensor.data, copy=True)
+            ).reshape(())
+            if not torch.isfinite(global_scale) or global_scale < 0:
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid NVFP4 GGUF global scale for {tensor.name}")
+            yield name, weight
+            yield name.removesuffix(".weight") + ".weight_scale", scale
+            yield name.removesuffix(".weight") + ".weight_scale_2", global_scale
+            continue
+        value = torch.from_numpy(np.array(tensor.data, copy=True))
+        if tensor.tensor_type == GGMLQuantizationType.BF16:
+            value = value.view(torch.bfloat16)
+        elif tensor.tensor_type != GGMLQuantizationType.F32:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unsupported LiLiCorr GGUF tensor type: {tensor.tensor_type}"
+            )
+        if name == "lilicorr.attention_bias.bias":
+            relative, same = slot_bias_from_gguf(
+                value, config.block_size, head["lilicorr_candidate_topk"]
+            )
+            yield "lilicorr.relative_slot_bias", relative
+            yield "lilicorr.same_slot_bias", same
+        elif name == "lilicorr.slot_embedding":
+            yield name, value.reshape(1, 1, config.block_size - 1, 1, -1)
+        elif name == "lilicorr.rank_embedding":
+            yield name, value.reshape(1, 1, 1, head["lilicorr_candidate_topk"], -1)
+        else:
+            yield name, value

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`lru_cache` keeps each parsed `GGUFReader` alive for the life of the process. The reader holds every metadata part as a NumPy view, so the drafter's tokenizer metadata stays in host memory after config and weight loading finish. The main process (`_resolve_speculative_algorithm_alias` -> `get_config`) and the scheduler each keep one. `build_gguf_tokenizer` now also caches the reader for GGUF-native targets such as muse-glimmer, in every process that builds the tokenizer.

**Example**

On a synthetic GGUF with the drafter's 131k tokens and 269k merges, one live reader adds about 470 MB RSS. Freeing it releases about 400 MB.

**Fix**

Cache the small derived results (architecture, LiLiCorr check, built config) instead of the reader, and let `lilicorr_gguf_weights` open a short-lived reader. Or call `get_gguf_reader.cache_clear()` once loading finishes.
